newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Oct 17.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Shares ended firmer on Thursday, buoyed by the return of bid speculation in drugs group Zeneca but after a session largely dominated by U.S. events. The FTSE 100 index finished up 17.7 points at 4,042.1, towards the top of the day's trading range. Advancers led decliners by roughly five-to-four.

FRANKFURT- Shares closed bourse trade mixed despite another record-breaking session on Wall Street overnight, weighed down by the weaker dollar in early European trade. The DAX index of 30 leading German shares closed 1.36 points up at 2,716.26 as the dollar fell below the 1.5400 marks level for the first time in recent trading days. In post bourse trade the Dax stood at 2717.50 up 12.44.

PARIS - French stocks rose on Thursday to finish close to Tuesday's year high, helped by a firm opening on Wall Street and U.S. data that suggested the economy was not overheating. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 6.81 points, or 0.32 percent, at 2,165.33, while the CAC-40 futures contract rose nine points to 2,167.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended marginally higher but failed to overcome the level of 3,800 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) in quiet trade and on moderate volumes. News that Russian president Yeltsin sacked security chief Alexander Lebed pressured prices in the last half hour of the session. Dealers said U.S. economic data had little influence. The SMI was up 0.08 percent, or 3.0 points, to 3,793.2. The Broad SPI rose 2.57 points to 2,432.92.

TOKYO - Stocks ended a shade higher after wandering narrowly in both negative and positive territory throughout the day. Brokers said investors were waiting for the Lower House of parliament elections which will be held on Sunday. The 225-issue Nikkei average inched up 26.55 points to 21,423.74.

HONG KONG - Stocks fought off bouts of profit-taking, rallying to a strong close led by continued strength in the banking sector. The Hang Seng Index fluctuated throughout the day in a 100-point range, closing up 40.62 points at 12,436.80. Turnover was a healthy HK$6.87 billion, although substantially down from Wednesday's HK$9.142 billion.

SYDNEY - Shares closed weaker, the market drifting lower after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) dampened expectations of a rate cut in its monthly bulletin released on Wednesday. The All Ordinaries index closed 11.2 points lower at 2,353.8, just off its intra-day low of 2,349.1.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares closed off worst levels in fairly active trade, with industrials retracing some losses on U.S. economic data and golds down on a weak bullion price. Dealers said the jobless claims figures in the U.S. which were largely in line with forecasts pointed to a softening economy and improved sentiment in U.S. bonds. The overall index fell 14.8 points to 7,008.1 points, industrials lost 7.8 points to 8,252.4 points and golds were off 11.9 points to 1,683.2 points.
